results.lastReply:
A VPN (virtual private network) is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Your traffic goes through the VPN company's computer first, and it is scrambled on the way so others on the network can't read it.

Websites then see the VPN company's address instead of yours, which hides your location and makes it harder to track you. It's most useful on public Wi-Fi at cafés, airports and hotels, where strangers share the same network.

A VPN isn't a cloak of invisibility. The VPN company can still see your activity, so pick one you trust, and avoid free ones that earn money by selling your data. It also won't protect you from scam links or weak passwords.

results.lastReply:
VPN (virtual private network) internet par ek private raasta hai, jo aapke phone ya laptop ko VPN company ke computer se jodta hai. Aapka data us raaste se guzarte waqt scramble ho jaata hai, isliye same Wi-Fi par koi aur use padh nahi sakta.

Websites ko aapka asli address nahi dikhta, sirf VPN company ka dikhta hai. Isse aapki location chhupti hai aur tracking mushkil hoti hai. Café, airport aur hotel ke public Wi-Fi par ye sabse zyada kaam aata hai.

VPN aapko bilkul invisible nahi banata. VPN company aapki activity dekh sakti hai, to bharosemand company chuniye aur aise free VPN se bachiye jo aapka data bechkar kamate hain. Ye scam links ya kamzor password se bhi nahi bachata.
